name: Single-agent Cisplatin Concurrent with Radiation (Vulvar SCC Chemoradiation)
stage: locally advanced (unresectable or requiring organ-preserving chemoradiation)

biomarkers.note: Single-agent cisplatin as a radiosensitizer is not biomarker gated. PD-L1 and MSI-H/dMMR are tested to guide later immunotherapy in advanced/recurrent disease, not this chemoradiation.

lineOfTherapy: primary treatment of locally advanced vulvar SCC; radiosensitizing chemotherapy given concurrently with external-beam radiation (definitive, or neoadjuvant to enable surgery)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: locally advanced vulvar squamous cell carcinoma treated with concurrent chemoradiation
eligibilityCriteria.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Vulvar Cancer (Squamous Cell Carcinoma)
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, Systemic Therapy for Vulvar Cancer, Chemoradiation: Cisplatin (single agent); footnote (Concurrent platinum-containing chemotherapy with EBRT utilizes cisplatin as a single agent, or carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant)

drugs.name: CISplatin

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Vulvar Cancer (Squamous Cell Carcinoma)
provenance.locator: Systemic Therapy for Vulvar Cancer, Chemoradiation column: Cisplatin (single agent; Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant); regimen named but per-dose number not printed

drugs.notes: Single-agent CISplatin is the radiosensitizing chemotherapy given concurrently with EBRT for locally advanced vulvar SCC (NCCN v2.2026; DeVita 12th ed. Table 49.5, GOG 101 and GOG 205, uses cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiation, lines 173422 to 173464). NEITHER cited source prints the cisplatin dose, basis, unit, or schedule; all set to VERIFY. For clinical context only (not asserted here as the vulvar dose): the analogous cervical radiosensitizing schedule is weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 (DeVita line 170910). Requires hydration and nephro/oto/neuro monitoring; carboplatin substitutes if cisplatin intolerant. Tall man per ISMP.

premedications.name: Cisplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: IV hydration before and after cisplatin; antiemetic prophylaxis for the platinum agent.

supportiveCare: cisplatin hydration protocol (pre- and post-infusion) to reduce nephrotoxicity.
aggressive local skin care and management of additive chemoradiation acute toxicity.

monitoring: renal function (creatinine, electrolytes/Mg) before each dose
audiometry/otologic and peripheral-neuropathy assessment for cisplatin
weekly review of concurrent radiation acute toxicity (local skin, GU/GI)

doseModificationRules.condition: rising creatinine, electrolyte derangement, or grade 2+ cisplatin toxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold cisplatin or switch to carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant per NCCN; physician decides.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: Table 49.5 Preoperative and Definitive Chemoradiation Studies in Advanced Vulvar Cancer, GOG 101 and GOG 205 (cisplatin-based concurrent chemoradiation), lines 173422 to 173464; the systemic chemotherapy dose is not tabulated

guideline.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Vulvar Cancer (Squamous Cell Carcinoma)
guideline.locator: Systemic Therapy for Vulvar Cancer, Chemoradiation: Cisplatin (single agent; Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant); primary-treatment concurrent-chemotherapy footnote

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for single-agent cisplatin concurrent with radiation for locally advanced vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (StewardMD reference disease vulvar_cancer, subtype #48). The regimen identity and curative concurrent-chemoradiation setting are grounded to Standard Guidelines (NCCN) Vulvar Cancer v2.2026 (Chemoradiation: single-agent Cisplatin, or Carboplatin if cisplatin intolerant) and DeVita 12th ed. Table 49.5 (GOG 101 and GOG 205 cisplatin-based chemoradiation, lines 173422 to 173464). However, NEITHER cited source prints the cisplatin dose, basis, unit, schedule, or cycle count; therefore cisplatin basis/dosePerUnit/unit/days plus cycleLengthDays and cycles are set to VERIFY and listed in verifyFields, pending a dosing source. No dose was invented or inferred (the weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 cervical radiosensitizing schedule is cited only as clinical context for the verifier). Cisplatin requires hydration with nephro-, oto-, and neurotoxicity monitoring. Tall man per ISMP. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
